name: sixteen3_gpu_tensor_kernel

phase_0.boundary_condition: The CUDA kernel launch boundary that encapsulates the batched evaluation of N registers over the fixed 4-lane boolean vector, containing the entire computation within a single GPU thread block execution.

⊢.justification: Represents the void state before the (N,4) boolean tensor is allocated or loaded into GPU global memory, the empty set of registers prior to kernel invocation.

⊣.justification: The terminal anchor representing the completion of the kernel launch and the synchronization point where all N threads have finished their elementwise operations.

≻.justification: The directed transformation where the fixed opcode (e.g., union, meet_t) is applied forward across the batch, propagating the logical operation from input tensor to output tensor.

≺.justification: The reverse morphism corresponding to the fixed permutations (truth_swap, info_swap, invol) that reorder the 4 lanes, effectively reversing the information flow direction within the register structure.

⋈.justification: The composition of multiple gate operations (e.g., meet_t followed by join_c) chained sequentially within the same kernel or across dependent kernel launches.

⊙.justification: The identity operation where a register's 4-lane state is read and written back unchanged, representing the self-reference of the Reg16_3 struct within the batch.

∈.justification: The co-multiplication that splits the single batched execution context into two parallel logical arms: one for the T-arm (affirmative lanes T,t) and one for the F-arm (negative lanes F,f) based on the specific gate logic.

∋.justification: The multiplication that reconstitutes the processed T-arm and F-arm results into a single unified 4-lane output register, resolving the parallel lane computations into one verdict.

⊤.justification: The evaluation of the constructive truth arm, specifically activating the T and t lanes within the boolean vector to compute the affirmative component of the lattice operation.

⊥.justification: The evaluation of the constructive falsity arm, specifically activating the F and f lanes within the boolean vector to compute the negative component of the lattice operation.

⊞.justification: The simultaneous holding of both affirmative and negative states (B value) within a register, representing a contradiction or dual activation that is preserved without resolution in the batched output.

⊡.justification: The irreversible fixation of the computed batched result into GPU global memory, creating a permanent, append-only record of the kernel's output tensor.

phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: The uninitialized GPU memory block where the (N,4) tensor has not yet been allocated or populated with boolean values.
phase_3.true_description: A register state where the T lane is set to 1 and all other lanes are 0, representing a constructively proven affirmative value across the batch.
phase_3.false_description: A register state where the F lane is set to 1 and all other lanes are 0, representing a constructively refuted negative value across the batch.
phase_3.both_description: A register state where both T and F lanes are set to 1 simultaneously, representing a dialetheic contradiction held live within the batched computation.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the void state for the GPU tensor block before any data is loaded.
Split the batched execution context into parallel T-arm and F-arm processing lanes.
Activate the affirmative computation path for the T and t lanes within the batch.
Apply the forward morphism of the selected gate (e.g., union) to the T-arm lanes.
Activate the negative computation path for the F and f lanes within the batch.
Apply the reverse morphism (lane permutation) to the F-arm lanes if required by the gate.
Rejoin the T-arm and F-arm results into a single unified 4-lane register output.
Hold the resulting B-state (both true and false) if the gate logic produces a contradiction.
Chain the output of this gate to the input of the next gate in the sequence.
Perform a self-reference check on the register state to verify identity preservation.
Commit the final computed tensor to global GPU memory as an immutable record.
Close the kernel execution boundary and synchronize all threads.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: nvcc CUDA compiler translating the IMASM token sequence into PTX assembly for the RTX 4070/3060 hardware.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Shared memory and global memory barriers within the CUDA thread block for inter-thread communication.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: GPU global memory storing the (N,4) boolean tensor as uint8 or bool arrays.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: CUDA runtime scheduler determining the launch configuration (grid/block dimensions) for the batched kernel.
phase_5.alfs_store: The imasm_core::imasm16_3 scalar CPU implementation serving as the canonical reference for gate correctness.

phase_6.cycle_cost: GPU compute cycles and memory bandwidth consumed per elementwise operation across the batch.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Input tensor with N registers in arbitrary SIXTEEN_3 states.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Output tensor with N registers transformed by the fixed gate logic.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The operation is a fixed, data-independent permutation and elementwise boolean logic, preserving the total information content of the batch without loss or generation of new entropy.
